goldens.comment: In UsernameForm.authenticate(), isConditionalPasskeysEnabled() is called without passing the required UserModel parameter.
goldens.reasoning: G1 is about a missing argument in the call in UsernameForm.authenticate(), which would be a compile error. C1 is about UsernamePasswordForm and the inverted user-null logic, not a missing argument.

goldens.comment: With isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(UserModel user) requiring user != null, authenticate(...) will not call webauthnAuth.fillContextForm(context) on the initial login page where context.getUser() is still null, so conditional passkey UI will not be set up for first-time passkey login. Consider whether this should also be enabled when no user has been selected yet so ID-less passkey authentication on the initial login form continues to work.
goldens.reasoning: C1 points out that requiring user != null means fillContextForm is never called on the first login, when no user is set yet, so the conditional passkey UI is lost. That is the same issue as G2.

candidates: services/src/main/java/org/keycloak/authentication/authenticators/browser/UsernamePasswordForm.java:161 - Passkey check is inverted: it now needs a user, so first login never gets conditional passkeys.. `isConditionalPasskeysEnabled` returns true only when `user != null`. The old code filled the WebAuthn data when no user was selected (`context.getUser() == null`). Both `authenticate()` (line 115) and `challenge(context, error, field)` (line 137) now call this helper, so a normal first login with no user identified never calls `webauthnAuth.fillContextForm`. The login page loses the conditional passkey UI and the `webauth` form, and it also loses them after a failed password attempt. The tests in this PR expect that form on the first login page (e.g. PasskeysUsernamePasswordFormTest lines 196 and 238). The `user != null` term also shows passkeys on re-authentication to users who have no passkey credential. Fix: enable passkeys when no user is selected, or when the selected user has a passwordless credential, e.g. `webauthnAuth != null && webauthnAuth.isPasskeysEnabled() && (user == null || user.credentialManager().isConfiguredFor(webauthnAuth.getCredentialType()))`.
